kelantan.title: Most people evacuated
kelantan.tagline: River floodplain upstream of the delta

facts.text: On 29 Nov 2024 Pasir Mas had the most evacuees in Kelantan: 22,486.

drivers.text: Rain is the trigger: monsoon surges filled the Kelantan River, which drains most of the state.
Land use upstream adds runoff, but in river modelling, changes in rain had about 3–4 times the effect of land-use change. So we never say forest loss causes the floods.

kelantan.ai_focus: The 5 Dec count comes from the other radar track, which sees the land from a different angle. Compare 29 Nov with 11 Dec (same track) before saying exactly how fast the water went down.
kelantan.ai_draft: Our radar map shows about 4,680 ha of new flood water in Pasir Mas on 29 Nov 2024 (range 4,137–4,680 ha), about 8% of the district. It arrived right after the three wettest days, 26–28 Nov, when about 127, 132 and 120 mm of rain fell per day. By 5 Dec only 786 ha was left, and by 17 Dec 235 ha, so most of the water drained within a week.

kelantan.title: Low delta by the sea

facts.text: On 29 Nov 2024 Tumpat had 11,105 evacuees, the second highest in Kelantan.

drivers.text: The coast is the bottleneck: flood risk rises when heavy rain meets high tides, which slow drainage of the flat delta.

kelantan.ai_focus: Check whether the water that stayed after 5 Dec sits in the same low fields each time. If it does, those fields are the slowest to drain and worth watching in the next monsoon.
kelantan.ai_draft: Tumpat had the largest share of its land under new flood water of any study district: about 3,596 ha on 29 Nov 2024, close to 20% of the district. The water also lingered. On 5 Dec about 1,330 ha remained, 37% of the peak, while upstream Pasir Mas kept only 17%. That fits a low delta where the river meets the tide.

kelantan.title: Where the river meets the sea
kelantan.tagline: State capital at the river mouth

facts.text: The Kelantan River basin covers about 12,000–13,000 km², more than 85% of the state, and overflows regularly from November to February.
On 1 Dec 2024, 97,128 people in Kelantan were affected, from 30,017 families.

drivers.text: Towns are hard for radar: flooded streets can look bright, not dark, so town pixels are marked unreliable.

kelantan.ai_focus: That rise on 11 Dec is probably not a second flood. 5 Dec and 11 Dec come from two different radar tracks with different viewing angles. Check it against NASA's water map for the same dates before reading it as new water.
kelantan.ai_draft: Kota Bharu shows about 2,404 ha of new flood water on 29 Nov 2024 (range 1,949–2,404 ha), about 6% of the district, all of it outside the built-up centre. Inside the town the radar cannot judge flooding, so built-up areas are greyed out, not counted as dry. The count drops to 37 ha on 5 Dec, then rises to 692 ha on 11 Dec.

kedah.title: Heart of the rice bowl

facts.text: The MADA granary grows about 37% of Malaysia's rice.
Season 2/2026 covers 99,489 ha in three phases, starting 23 Sep, 3 Oct and 13 Oct.

drivers.text: People flood the fields on a schedule set by dam water and rain, before seeding.

kedah.ai_focus: About 7,259 ha first showed water only on 31 Oct. Look at whether those fields lie far from the main canals, which would point to water reaching them last.
kedah.ai_draft: Only about 1% of Kota Setar's rice land showed water in the fields on 23–25 Sep 2026, even though MADA's Phase I began on 23 Sep. Field water grew to about 5% by 5–7 Oct, 17–20% by 17–19 Oct and 46.7% by 31 Oct. Most fields first got water after Phase III began on 13 Oct, which suggests planting ran late in this drought year. The biggest jump came after the wettest day of the season, 25 Oct, with about 114 mm of rain.

kedah.title: Northern paddy belt
kedah.tagline: About a third of our Kedah radar area

facts.text: Kubang Pasu covers about 31% of our Kedah radar area, the largest share of any district (our measurement from DOSM boundaries).
We found no MADA map of which blocks belong to which phase, so timing is checked against the whole schedule.

drivers.text: Irrigation this season depends on rain: dams stood at 35.76% on 17 Sep 2026.

kedah.ai_focus: About 8,696 ha first showed water on 17–19 Oct. Compare those fields with MADA's Phase II and III areas to see whether water reached them on time.
kedah.ai_draft: Kubang Pasu, the biggest of our three focus districts by rice land, got water earlier than Kota Setar: 8.7% of its rice land by 5 Oct 2026 against 5.1%. By 31 Oct it reached 55.1%, the highest of the three districts. The two NISAR tracks agree on the trend but differ by a few points on nearby dates (32.6% on 17 Oct, 28% on 19 Oct), which shows how much the viewing angle matters.

kedah.title: Inland edge of the granary
kedah.tagline: Only partly inside our radar area

facts.text: About 63% of Pendang lies inside our radar area; the rest has no radar data in this prototype (our measurement).
By 13 Oct 2026 MADA dam storage had risen to 40.13%.

drivers.text: Smooth dry soil can look like water to radar, so a drought year raises the risk of false alarms.

kedah.ai_focus: The early 'wet' patches may be smooth, dry soil, which can look like water to radar, rather than real field water. Check whether the same patches stay dark on every pass: real flooding comes and goes with planting.
kedah.ai_draft: Pendang looks different from the other two districts. About 6.8% of its rice land already looked wet on 23 Sep 2026, the day MADA's Phase I began, yet it only reached 20.9% by 31 Oct. Only 63% of the district lies inside our radar area.

items.text: Smooth water in a field sends the flat echo away: HH turns dark (plan 04 §4.5).

items.name: HV dark-water test
items.text: HV must also be dark, which separates water from young plants.
